note: Provider acceptance worksheet for the shipped subsets. It separates what the automated synthetic checks already prove from what only a user-approved live run can prove. No account has been connected and no test object has been sent to create these rows: every live field is empty and must be filled by the account owner. Automated results never imply live acceptance, and a fixture cannot fill a live field.
how_to_use: Work one service at a time, and one account at a time, only after the maintainer approves a live acceptance task.
Follow the numbered steps for that service from install through disconnect, and record the outcome of each one.
Use a user-owned token of the documented type with the least permission recorded in connectors/SETUP.md, and record the token type and expiry, never the token itself.
Record the API version in use and the date, because both the wire shape and the reviewed source can change.
Leave case as synthetic unless a real account was really used. A synthetic fixture is never upgraded to live by editing this file.
For an uncertain write, record how it was checked in the service's own UI rather than resending.
If a step fails, record the failure rather than working around it, and leave later live fields empty.

providers.least_permission: A Todoist personal API token from Settings, Integrations, Developer. It is account-wide and cannot be scoped per project, so the subset keeps its authority minimal by reading selected IDs, bounding listings to three cursor pages, and creating only reviewed Inbox tasks.

synthetic_expectations.identity_result: subject 1234567 from /id and label from /email, with the account's own echoed token field never leaving identity selection
synthetic_expectations.read_result: read_task returns id and content; read_task_detail also returns description; read_project returns id, name, is_shared and is_favorite; list_tasks and list_projects stop at three pages and report more_available
synthetic_expectations.reviewed_create_preview: POST /api/v1/tasks with exactly content and description, an omitted project_id so the task lands in the Inbox, and a payload_sha256 over the reviewed bytes
synthetic_expectations.uncertain_write_handling: A create that fails after dispatch is reported as uncertain and never replayed; the Inbox is checked by hand
synthetic_expectations.disconnect_and_revoke: Disconnecting in Steed removes the stored credential; the token is revoked in the same Todoist settings screen

steps: Install connectors/recipes/todoist.json from App Connections, read the source review and install it.
Connect a synthetic account check: create a Todoist personal API token in Settings, Integrations, Developer and paste it into the Connect step.
Enable only the actions you want this account to offer to tasks.
Run read_task for a known task ID, then read_task_detail, then read_project and list_projects, and record the returned fields.
Run list_tasks and record how many pages were returned and whether more_available was true.
Create a draft, review the exact payload and payload hash, approve it, and record the created task id and whether it landed in the Inbox.
Record the receipt the tool returned, including the created task id, and read the task back to see the stored result.
If the create was uncertain, check the Inbox by hand and record how you checked.
Disconnect the account, confirm the stored credential is gone, then revoke the token in Todoist.

providers.reviewed_source: connectors/recipes/templates/github-owner-template.json, imported as a user-owned copy with the owner and repository fixed
providers.least_permission: A fine-grained personal access token with a short expiry, repository access limited to the one repository in the reviewed source, and Issues read and write only. No contents, pull request, actions or administration permission, and no account permissions.

synthetic_expectations.identity_result: subject from the numeric /id and label from /login, never from a private email
synthetic_expectations.read_result: read_issue returns number, title, state, state_reason and body, with documented nullable fields passed through as explicit nulls, and the same projection for a pull request because the object type is not established
synthetic_expectations.reviewed_create_preview: POST /repos/{owner}/{repository}/issues with exactly title and body, and a payload_sha256 over the reviewed bytes
synthetic_expectations.uncertain_write_handling: A create that fails after dispatch is reported as uncertain and never replayed; the repository issue list is checked by hand
synthetic_expectations.disconnect_and_revoke: Disconnecting in Steed removes the stored credential; the token is revoked on the fine-grained tokens page

steps: Install your own copy: copy connectors/recipes/templates/github-owner-template.json, replace the owner and repository placeholders, and import it with Add Connector Recipe.
Connect with a fine-grained token created for that one repository with a short expiry and Issues read and write only.
Enable the actions you want this account to offer to tasks.
Run read_repository, then read_issue for a known issue number, and record the returned fields including any documented nulls.
Create a draft, review the exact payload, approve it, and record the created issue number and URL.
Read the issue again by its number to see the created result; record that this confirming read was manual and is not automatic reconciliation.
Record the receipt the tool returned, including the created issue number and URL, and read that issue back to see the stored result; that confirming read is manual, not automatic reconciliation.
If the create was uncertain, check the repository issue list and record how you checked.
Disconnect the account, confirm the credential is gone, then revoke the token on the fine-grained tokens page.

providers.reviewed_source: connectors/recipes/gitlab.json, plus connectors/recipes/templates/gitlab-project-template.json imported as a user-owned copy with the numeric project ID fixed
providers.least_permission: A GitLab personal access token with a short expiry. read_api for reads only, or api when reviewed issue creation is wanted, because issue creation is not available to read_api.

synthetic_expectations.identity_result: subject from the numeric /id and label from /username
synthetic_expectations.read_result: read_project returns id, path_with_namespace and web_url for one numeric project ID; the per-project template's read_issue returns iid, title, state, description and web_url for one issue IID, with a documented null description passed through as an explicit null and no tier-conditional field projected
synthetic_expectations.reviewed_create_preview: POST /api/v4/projects/{id}/issues with exactly title and description, a tool description warning that a command starting a line of the description is a quick action, and a payload_sha256 over the reviewed bytes
synthetic_expectations.uncertain_write_handling: Nothing in this subset can prove a create committed, so the issue list is checked by hand and nothing is resent
synthetic_expectations.disconnect_and_revoke: Disconnecting in Steed removes the stored credential; the token is revoked on the access tokens page

steps: Install connectors/recipes/gitlab.json, or install a copy of the per-project template with your numeric project ID when you want issue reads.
Connect a token created with a short expiry and the narrowest scope you need: read_api for reads, api for reviewed issue creation.
Enable the actions you want this account to offer to tasks.
Run read_project for a numeric project ID, then read_issue for a known issue IID, and record the returned fields.
Create a draft whose description starts a line with a slash command, review the exact payload, approve it, and record the created issue IID and URL.
Confirm in GitLab what the quick-action line actually did; the profile sends it unchanged and does not strip or guess it.
Record the receipt the tool returned, including the created issue IID and URL, then read that issue back to see the stored result.
If the create was uncertain, check the issue list and record how you checked.
Disconnect the account, confirm the credential is gone, then revoke the token on the access tokens page.

providers.least_permission: An Asana personal access token, which carries exactly the access of the user who created it, so the narrowest reduction is a dedicated account limited to the projects or tasks intended for reading. Asana documents personal access tokens as persistent by default with no documented expiry, so the token must be revoked manually.

synthetic_expectations.identity_result: subject from the numeric /data/gid and label from /data/name, never from the opt-in /data/email
synthetic_expectations.read_result: read_project returns gid, name, notes, archived, due_on, owner and permalink_url; read_task returns gid, name, notes, completed, due_on, assignee and permalink_url. Every projected field is one Asana does not mark [Opt In], and no opt-in or html_notes field is projected.
synthetic_expectations.reviewed_create_preview: none: the profile is read-only, because Asana names the workspace or project in a create body rather than in the path
synthetic_expectations.uncertain_write_handling: not applicable while no write is offered
synthetic_expectations.disconnect_and_revoke: Disconnecting in Steed removes the stored credential; the token is revoked from the same Asana account page

steps: Install connectors/recipes/asana.json from App Connections, read the source review and install it.
Connect with a personal access token created in Asana and pasted into the Connect step.
Enable only the read actions you want this account to offer to tasks.
Run read_project and read_task for known GIDs taken from the Asana URLs, and record the returned fields.
Confirm the identity result shows your account name rather than an opt-in email field.
Disconnect the account, confirm the credential is gone, then deauthorize the token from My Apps.

providers.least_permission: A Raindrop.io access token or test token. No scope is documented for reads, so the narrowest reduction is a token used only for collection reads and revoked when it is no longer needed.

synthetic_expectations.identity_result: subject from the integer /user/_id and label from /user/fullName
synthetic_expectations.read_result: read_collection returns the documented _id, title, count and view through the item wrapper; list_root_collections returns the documented item objects under /items, with no paging followed
synthetic_expectations.reviewed_create_preview: none: a bookmark create needs an explicit link input that no reviewed destination can carry
synthetic_expectations.uncertain_write_handling: not applicable while no write is offered
synthetic_expectations.disconnect_and_revoke: Disconnecting in Steed removes the stored credential; the token is revoked in the Raindrop app console

steps: Install connectors/recipes/raindrop.json from App Connections, read the source review and install it.
Connect an access token or test token copied from the App Management Console and pasted into the Connect step.
Enable only the read actions you want this account to offer to tasks.
Run read_collection for a collection ID from a collection URL, then list_root_collections, and record the returned fields.
Confirm what a failed read looks like in your account so the recorded behaviour matches the documented result flag.
Disconnect the account, confirm the credential is gone, then revoke the token in the app console.

providers.reviewed_source: connectors/recipes/templates/zotero-library-template.json imported as a user-owned copy with the numeric library ID fixed
providers.least_permission: A Zotero API key used with Authorization: Bearer. The identity document carries an access object whose user.library flag must be true; no write permission is needed for this read-only subset, and no key may be placed in a URL.

synthetic_expectations.identity_result: subject from the numeric userID and label from username
synthetic_expectations.read_result: read_item returns key, version, itemType, dateAdded and dateModified for one item key, with no title projected because a note has none
synthetic_expectations.uncertain_write_handling: not applicable while no write is offered
synthetic_expectations.disconnect_and_revoke: Disconnecting in Steed removes the stored credential; the key is revoked on the Zotero API Keys page

steps: Install your own copy: copy connectors/recipes/templates/zotero-library-template.json, replace the numeric library ID, and import it with Add Connector Recipe.
Confirm in the source review that the pinned library ID is disclosed as user-supplied and unchecked.
Connect a Zotero API key pasted into the Connect step.
Enable the read action you want this account to offer to tasks.
Run read_item for a known item key and record the returned fields, noting that no title is returned.
Open a second library you can access and record what read_item returns for it, so the unchecked mismatch risk is a recorded fact rather than a claim.
Disconnect the account, confirm the credential is gone, then revoke the key on the API Keys page.

providers.least_permission: A delegated Microsoft Graph access token that the user obtains with their own tooling, requesting only User.Read, Files.Read, Calendars.Read and Tasks.Read. An application token must not be used, because /me requires a delegated token.

synthetic_expectations.identity_result: subject from the not-nullable /id and label from /userPrincipalName, never from a mail field whose nullability is not formally documented
synthetic_expectations.read_result: read_drive_item returns id, name, webUrl, size and lastModifiedDateTime for both a file and a folder, since the file and folder facets are absent rather than null; the two collection reads return only /value from the first page and never follow @odata.nextLink
synthetic_expectations.uncertain_write_handling: not applicable while no write is offered
synthetic_expectations.disconnect_and_revoke: Disconnecting in Steed removes the stored token immediately; the delegated token itself is revoked or expires according to the user's own tooling

steps: Install connectors/recipes/microsoft365-read.json from App Connections, read the source review and install it.
Connect a delegated access token you obtained yourself for your own account with only the documented read scopes; an application token will not work.
Enable the reads you want this account to offer to tasks.
Run read_drive_item with a driveItem ID taken from a Graph response, not from a sharing URL or encoded sharing token.
Run the calendar and To Do reads and record that only the first page was returned and that no next link was followed.
Disconnect the account, confirm the token is gone from Steed, then revoke it or let it expire according to your own tooling.

live_acceptance_preconditions: A maintainer-approved live acceptance task, naming the account, the reviewed source and the permission scope.
A user-owned token supplied by the account owner; no credential is ever committed or pasted into a recipe.
Agreement on what may be created in the real account, and on cleaning it up afterwards.
Confirmation that no completion, delete, administrative or unrelated effect is in scope for any case.
step_order: reviewed draft and write, for services that offer one
receipt and follow-up read, when a write was made
live_fields_may_not_be_filled_from_fixtu: A synthetic result belongs in synthetic_expectations only. Live fields stay empty until an operator explicitly authorizes and completes the steps against a real account.
step_order_note: A read-only service has fewer steps than phases: the write and receipt phases are recorded as not applicable rather than padded with filler.
